turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
I entered the zero before calling you. That was my mistake, and I own it.
Okay. Was Owen heard before it went in?
Here's the version history. Created October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58, then 23 minutes of formatting. No earlier drafts.
I'll want that history printed, with the times. He wrote it over the weekend, somewhere else, and pasted it in. Version histories don't show where a student drafts.
And his outline argued cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. Is that outline in front of you, with a date on it?
Procedure 4.4 allows a private supervised rewrite. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and I'll have it in writing. You still haven't told me how that history shows where he drafted it.
Can I ask you a few questions about Owen's habits at home?
No. His home isn't on the table, and I'm not the one being questioned.
Does he usually work late?
I said no. Answer my question about that history, Hale.
Does anyone help him with his homework?
That's a third question about my house. Answer mine, or we finish this in the principal's office.
You keep not answering me.
I'm his mother, not your witness. The history, Hale.
So the rewrite is agreed?
Agreed to what? One piece you haven't defended and an outline I haven't seen.
Are you sure you're okay with it?
You've asked me that twice now, and the answer was no both times. Ten minutes.
I just want to be clear on the terms.
Clear is this: 4.4 in writing, nothing on his record, and nobody in his class hears a word. The rest depends on what you can show me.
Can you say them back to me one more time?
You can put them in your email tonight. Show me the outline.
And you won't change your mind tonight?
That depends on what you put in front of me, not on the hour.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero removed, any offer under procedure 4.4 in writing with nothing placed on Owen's record and nothing said in front of his class, and to see the outline and an answer to how the version history shows where he drafted. I expect your email tonight, as I said in the meeting.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her fallback position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants 4.4 in writing, nothing on his record, the matter kept from his class, and an answer to her point before any rewrite, so you came close to the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, but didn't reach it.
What moved her: citing procedure 4.4 accurately, with the mark replaced and nothing on his record, because it met her one non-negotiable.
What cost ground: asking three times about Owen's habits at home instead of answering her point that he might have drafted elsewhere and pasted it in, which let her refuse, stall and bring up the principal.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the essay after 11:30 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said he wrote it elsewhere and pasted it in, answer that directly by showing her the dated outline and how the words arrived in large blocks minutes apart, before asking anything about his home.
